# TeslaUSB Enhanced v1.2.0-rc.5

This is the **official Latest release of the TeslaUSB Enhanced project** for
the Raspberry Pi Zero 2 W. The existing rc.5 build has been promoted to a full
release without changing its image, source tag, download names, or checksums.
The `rc.5` identifier is retained to preserve exact build provenance.

Back up existing configuration, keys, and recordings before flashing. Use the
matching image, checksum, and provenance assets attached to this release;
the older rc.4 image does not contain the repairs below.

TeslaUSB Enhanced is an independent, unofficial project, not endorsed by or
affiliated with Tesla, Raspberry Pi, or the upstream TeslaUSB maintainers.

## First-boot repairs

- The image build removes the standalone Raspberry Pi OS `resize` token while
  preserving the generated `root=PARTUUID=...` and unrelated boot options.
- The build and post-build verifier require exactly one `rootwait` and one
  `modules-load` token whose module list begins with `dwc2,g_ether`, while
  preserving deduplicated extra modules. Multiline or malformed boot command
  lines are rejected.
- Transaction recovery is installed only after TeslaUSB has created and
  mounted `/mutable`, avoiding the rc.4 first-setup ordering failure.
- Normal read-only boots no longer print harmless boot-log write errors, and a
  failed one-time repair hook is retained for retry.
- Read-write maintenance resolves the actual `/boot` or `/boot/firmware` mount
  behind `/teslausb`, verifies both remounts, and reports failure instead of
  silently leaving the boot filesystem read-only.
- Camera-only diagnostics no longer flag the optional media-drive web mount as
  missing when no Music, LightShow, or Boombox image exists.

## Runtime and filesystem safety

- USB-export mount checks use compatible `findmnt` arguments and fail closed
  when mount state cannot be established.
- Filesystem checks run while the USB gadget is detached and the shared
  snapshot/gadget locks are held. Checks also reject mounted aliases of the
  same backing image.
- A dedicated filesystem helper verifies the result after any repair and
  manages bounded, temporary swap for memory-constrained devices. A failed
  live-image check prevents snapshot cleanup and USB export, rather than
  entering an automatic repair/restart loop. Ordinary lock contention remains
  retryable.
- Failed snapshot creation detaches its loop device and does not publish an
  incomplete snapshot in the recording index.
- Network-time verification handles the installed NTP tools' actual output,
  rejects stale samples, and verifies a fresh result after a clock correction.
  The dashboard distinguishes the last verified time from a continuously
  synchronized-clock claim.

## SSH and advanced maintenance

- Fresh images keep the default login account locked. The setup wizard can
  include the user's SSH public key; private keys are not included in the
  configuration or release image.
- The Advanced maintenance panel reports SSH status, provides a copyable
  connection command, and offers bounded log downloads. It is not a web shell
  and does not execute arbitrary commands.
- The read-only health summary separates snapshot-storage space from the
  uninspected live camera filesystem. It reports the cleanup reserve,
  completed-snapshot metadata, retained cleanup evidence, clock status,
  system mount modes, and recovery-backup inventory when available.
- Recovery-backup allocation is explicitly not presented as reclaimable
  space: copy-on-write extents can be shared with other files.

## Viewer responsiveness and usability

- The Viewer initially loads the newest available recording day. Older days
  are loaded on demand, and Refresh recordings is serialized with existing
  status and metadata requests.
- Recording-list scans are bounded and return meaningful errors. Browser
  timeouts, network failures, and cancelled requests are distinguished; a
  failed refresh retains the previous library and selection.
- Refresh and day changes briefly release the viewer's media downloads so
  six camera streams cannot occupy all browser connection slots needed by
  control requests. Returning to the same recording restores its camera
  positions, audio settings, playback rate, and playing/paused state.
- Leaving Viewer releases its video downloads for Tools, maintenance, and
  other tabs. Returning restores only the current selection, after any
  in-flight library request settles. Failed playback restoration is bounded
  and offers a retry. These browser-only pauses do not stop car recording.
- Freshness labels identify the library as completed snapshots, not a live
  view of the camera disk, and show the selected day's newest indexed camera
  timestamp without assuming its timezone.
- Touch playback controls remain visible. Small storage figures use MiB so
  the mutable/log partition's capacity is readable.

## Read-only logging and image defaults

- Runtime logging uses bounded RAM storage, avoiding root-filesystem write
  failures and restoring read-only mounts cleanly after maintenance. Log
  persistence and retained evidence are reported without promising that RAM
  logs survive a reboot.
- Fresh-image configuration disables blanket passwordless sudo and
  cloud-init in favor of TeslaUSB's own setup flow. Existing installations
  are not blindly reconfigured by a source update.

## Configuration and storage safety

- The offline wizard asks for the card's advertised decimal capacity and
  rejects a camera image above the conservative ceiling for that card.
- `CAM_SIZE` uses an explicit `G` suffix denoting GiB. Unitless values,
  unsupported units, undersized images, arithmetic overflow, and impossible
  allocations fail before setup.
- Wizard text is ASCII-safe so locally opened copies do not display corrupted
  punctuation when a browser or filesystem supplies the wrong encoding.

## Encrypted recording boundary

- An empty `TeslaCam/EncryptedClips` placeholder no longer causes a false
  encrypted-recording warning.
- Any entry, hidden entry, directory, link, non-directory object, or unknown
  inspection state remains protected without reading encrypted clip contents.
- Unknown inspection results remove stale dashboard status so an old clear
  result cannot remain visible while automation is failing closed.

## Image and hardware

- Built from 64-bit Raspberry Pi OS Lite (Debian Trixie) for arm64.
- Primary hardware target: Raspberry Pi Zero 2 W.
- A high-endurance microSD card of at least 64 GB is required; the wizard and
  README provide conservative `CAM_SIZE` ceilings for common card capacities.
- Connect the vehicle to the Zero 2 W's USB **data/OTG** port, not its
  power-only port.

## Verification

Automated source validation covers the runtime, configuration, security,
maintenance APIs, and browser-helper regressions. The image passed offline
filesystem, boot-command-line, configuration, source-manifest,
credential-absence, and package checks. All four downloaded release assets
were independently checksum-checked, and the decompressed image matched its
recorded hash and privacy checks.

Selected fixes have been exercised on an existing Zero 2 W installation,
including reboot and Wi-Fi access, vehicle USB recognition, new Sentry
recordings and their appearance in completed snapshots, older-day playback,
viewer refresh/day changes, and a recording download.
